transitPass.title: Transit Refund Comparison: K-Pass, Modu Card, Climate Card
transitPass.subtitle: Enter your monthly fares and trips to compare K-Pass basic, Modu Card standard and Modu Card Plus refunds and see which one applies.

regionHint.seoul: Same thresholds as the capital area. Seoul residents get youth benefits up to age 39 through the Climate Pass (Modu Card).
regionHint.metro: Capital-area thresholds. Local extras such as Gyeonggi Pass or Incheon I-Pass are not included here.
regionHint.local: Outside the capital area. If you live in a depopulation area (priority or special support), choose that instead.
regionHint.pref: A depopulation area designated for priority support. Check your city or county by choosing your province on the Modu Card website.
regionHint.special: A depopulation area designated for special support. Check your city or county by choosing your province on the Modu Card website.

groupHint.general: Age 19 or older and none of the other types.
groupHint.youthSeoul: Age 19 to 34. Seoul residents count as youth up to 39 through the Climate Pass.
groupHint.senior: Age 65 or older. This type was added in 2026.
groupHint.kids2: Parents with 2 children, at least one aged 18 or under. Verify via 'Multi-child info' in My menu on the website.
groupHint.kids3: Parents with 3 or more children, at least one aged 18 or under. Verify via 'Multi-child info' in My menu on the website.
groupHint.low: Basic livelihood recipients and near-poverty households.

methodRule.basic: Refunds {rate}% of what you spend. Trips boarded in the off-peak windows get 30%p more.
methodRule.general: Refunds everything above ₩{base} spent on trips under ₩3,000.
methodRule.plus: Refunds everything above ₩{base} spent on all trips.

input.title: Your travel
input.fareHint: What you pay per journey, including transfers. The capital-area subway base fare (card) is ₩1,550.
input.fareErr: Enter ₩{min} to ₩{max}. Put fares of ₩3,000 or more in the field below.
input.tripsHint: A journey with transfers counts once. Commuting 5 days a week is about 44 trips a month.
input.amountHint: Your card app's transit total for last month is the most accurate.
input.wide: I also take trips of ₩3,000 or more, such as express buses, GTX or the Shinbundang Line
input.wideHint: Journeys costing ₩{fare} or more in total (including transfers) are excluded from Standard and count only for Plus.
input.wideFareHint: Total fare per journey, including transfers.
input.wideAmountHint: The part of your monthly spending on journeys of ₩3,000 or more, such as express buses or GTX.
input.wideAmountOver: This is more than your monthly total, so the monthly total is used.
input.offpeakHint: Trips boarded 5:30–6:30, 9–10, 16–17 or 19–20. Until {end}, the Basic refund rate is 30%p higher for these.

result.label: {method} applies · estimated refund
result.pay: You actually pay ₩{pay} a month (of ₩{total}) · ₩{year} refunded a year
result.under15: You need at least {min} trips a month for a refund. You have {trips}, so {need} more would qualify. The first month after signing up is refunded even with fewer than 15.
result.disclaimer: Estimated with the Modu Card website's calculation method. Actual refunds depend on your card records (transfers, fares), whether it is your first month and local extras.

bars.title: Three methods compared
bars.auto: You don't choose in advance. Each month all three are calculated from your spending and the largest refund is paid automatically.

breakeven.title: When a flat-rate plan wins
breakeven.at: At your current pattern, {method} beats Basic from ₩{amount} a month (₩{fare} average × {trips} trips).

already.general: Standard already wins. Spending on trips under ₩3,000 above ₩{base} is fully refunded, so extra trips like that cost you nothing more.
already.plus: Plus already wins. Everything you spend above ₩{base} is fully refunded.

breakeven.plusNow: Your ₩3,000+ trips (₩{wide}) exceed ₩{x}, so Plus beats Standard.
breakeven.plusAt: Plus beats Standard once ₩3,000+ trips exceed ₩{x} a month (now ₩{wide}).
breakeven.offpeak: Off-peak extras are counted for trips boarded until {end}. Whether they continue in 2027 has not been announced.

climate.title: What happened to the Climate Card
climate.ended: Seoul's 30-day Climate Card ended with trips on September 30, 2026 (prepaid top-ups until August 31). Since September 1, Seoul residents get the same kind of refund through the Climate Pass, which is based on the Modu Card. 1- to 7-day passes are still sold.
climate.compare: The old 30-day pass (₩62,000 general) worked mainly on Seoul subways and Seoul buses. Now you actually pay ₩{pay} of this month's ₩{total}, and the Shinbundang Line, express buses, GTX and transit in other regions also count.
climate.youth: Seoul residents count as youth up to age 39 (Basic 30%, Standard threshold ₩55,000).

howTo.title: How to sign up
items: Get a Modu Card (K-Pass) from a card company. Both debit and credit cards are available, and an existing K-Pass card keeps working.
Sign up and register your card on the Modu Card website (korea-pass.kr) or app before refunds start counting.
For the multi-child type, apply under 'Multi-child info' in My menu; the higher rate applies once verification is done.
Refunds go to your card company the month after you travel. Payment date and form (points, bill credit) depend on the card company.
Seoul residents get Climate Pass benefits automatically without a separate application.

caution.title: Things to watch
items: No refund with fewer than 15 trips a month (except your first month). Transfers count as one journey until your next first boarding.
Intercity, express and airport coaches, KTX and SRT, which need separate tickets, do not count.
Standard only counts journeys under ₩3,000 in total. Frequent express bus or GTX riders may get Plus instead.
The 60-trip monthly cap was removed in 2026, and there is no refund ceiling.
2027 thresholds, rates and any extension of the off-peak extra have not been announced. Check the website notices when they are.
Local extras such as Gyeonggi Pass or Incheon I-Pass are not included in this calculation.

items.q: Are K-Pass and Modu Card different cards?
items.a: They are the same program. From January 2026, flat-rate options (Modu Card Standard and Plus) were added to K-Pass, and existing K-Pass cards keep working. Each month Basic, Standard and Plus are all calculated and the largest refund applies automatically.

items.q: What is the difference between Standard and Plus?
items.a: Standard counts only journeys under ₩3,000 in total (including transfers); Plus counts everything, including express buses, GTX and the Shinbundang Line. Plus has a higher threshold (capital area general ₩62,000 vs ₩100,000).

items.q: Which is better, Climate Card or K-Pass?
items.a: The 30-day Climate Card ended on September 30, 2026, and Seoul residents moved to the Climate Pass based on the Modu Card. The old pass price (₩62,000 general) equals the capital-area Standard threshold, so heavy riders within Seoul never pay more than ₩62,000 and lighter months still get the Basic refund.

items.q: How many trips do I need for a refund?
items.a: At least 15 a month. Your first month after signing up is refunded even with fewer. The old 60-trip monthly cap was removed in 2026.

items.q: From what monthly amount does a flat-rate plan win for general users?
items.a: In the capital area with only sub-₩3,000 journeys, Standard starts to beat Basic above ₩77,500 a month (₩77,500 − ₩62,000 = ₩15,500, equal to 20% of ₩77,500). For youth it is about ₩78,571, for low income about ₩96,360.

items.q: Are the half-price thresholds from April to September still available?
items.a: No. The 2026 April–September threshold cut ended with September trips, and the regular thresholds apply from October 1. The off-peak extra continues until December 31, 2026.

items.q: What is the off-peak commuting extra?
items.a: Boarding 5:30–6:30, 9–10, 16–17 or 19–20 adds 30%p to the Basic rate (general 20% → 50%). It does not apply to the flat-rate methods and runs for trips boarded until December 31, 2026.
